newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian troops set off for Albania.
newsitem.headline: Romanian troops set off for Albania.

text.p: Romanian troops sailed off to Albania on Wednesday to join a multi-national force and oversee aid supplies to the troubled country.

"We might be deployed in the towns of Girocaster and Sarande," Colonel Sorin Ioan told Reuters as the 400 troops dressed in battle fatigues and armed with submachine guns boarded a ship in the Black Sea port of Constanta.

Earlier this month, Romania's parliament approved the dispatch of the troops to Albania to join a 6,000-strong Italian-led force from eight nations which aims to secure deliveries of humanitarian aid.
"We hope to have no problems," Ioan said.
In the latest episode of violence in Albania on Wednesday, at least 22 people died after an explosion at a military base outside the capital.
"Try not to resort to force," Chief of Staff General Constantin Degeratu told the troops in Constanta.

Several hundred people have been killed in Albania since unrest broke out at the end of February, when pyramid investment schemes which sucked in the savings of tens of thousands of Albanians collapsed.
Unofficial estimates say up to a million arms have been distributed among the 3.4 million population.
